title: Rewinding the counter head
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Boolean Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, choose Boolean forwarding and find modes, and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. Let $C$ be a base loop-host configuration on $x$, let $p$ be an input-head position, let $w$ be a Boolean word, and let $b$ be a Boolean success indicator. For every $j\le |w|$, running the host for $j+1$ steps from phase $9$ when $b$ is true or phase $10$ when $b$ is false, with empty flag and payload tracks, counter track holding $w$ and head at $j-1$, ends with the counter head at zero and the same counter word. The final control is the released next-anchor call when $b$ is true and phase $11$ otherwise; the input position and all other tracks retain the values prescribed by the frame.
hypotheses_covered: Forwarding and find modes are Boolean
$C$ is a base loop-host configuration on $x$
replaced:
Let $w$ be a counter word, $b$ a success bit, and $j \le |w|$. Running the loop host for
exactly $j + 1$ steps from the rewind phase selected by $b$ on a frame whose counter
track is the buffer tape of $w$ with head at cell $j - 1$ returns the counter head to
zero and dispatches: success releases the next anchor call, underflow enters the
exhaustion phase without yet emitting. All inactive residue is retained.
